judgements.justification: A's area chair made four 7s a spotlight citing only that 'all the reviewers' agreed; no A reviewer rated above 7, while B, with the only 8, was held at poster by its spread of 6s.
Reviewer_z1y4 and Reviewer_h4G7 raised to 7 on Mahalanobis and DUQ numbers copied from other papers, not rerun, which completed A's unanimous 7s.

A's two-sentence meta-review omits z1y4's 'somewhat limited' significance, h4G7's doubt on adoption and the last-layer-Laplace-only experiments; B's meta-review carried motivation and last-layer Laplace forward as remaining concerns.

The wrong checkable claims (FpoL on the unjustified motivation, aGgD on missing captions, YyKC on Meinke and Hein) did not lower or set a score; aGgD's praise of Fig. 6 read the figure as the paper presented it.
B's authors admitted the CIFAR-10-C loader bug and that the rerun left RGPR barely above LLL, yet Reviewer_oTxs raised to 8 and Reviewer_YyKC to 6; no B score went down.
Every objection in both committees came within the response period; the authors answered Reviewer_4z2v twice.
The reviews were not near-identical in substance: only B knew of the loader bug and the kernel ablation, and B's area chair cited specific open concerns, not only scores.
All A reviewers, including the confidence-4 z1y4, gave 7, so the chair followed no less-informed majority against them; B's chair cited its confidence-4 Reviewer_d2CF's concern.

A's main concerns (missing baselines, approximation rigor) were closed by new numbers and promises, lifting three A reviewers to 7; B's DSCS-motivation and infinite-ReLU framing concern could not be answered and held Reviewer_4z2v at 6.
Neither committee had an outlying score; A is uniform at 7 and B spans 6 to 8 without a lone outlier.
No outlying reviewer in either committee, and every reviewer replied to the response.
Neither area chair set aside a low outlying score or defended acceptance against a detractor.
No reviewer or area chair raised audience breadth or venue fit.
Both meta-reviews omit material (A the weaknesses, B the loader bug) but neither misstates the reviewers' final positions or which concerns the response answered.
All eight reviewers replied to the authors' response; aGgD's reply was one line but present.
Reviewer_aGgD (confidence 1, 1.5 hours, 'cursory glance', proofs unread) gave 7, which counted in full toward the unanimity behind A's spotlight.
Neither committee split between accept and reject; all eight final ratings are 6 or above.
Only B was told of the CIFAR-10-C loader bug, given the corrected rerun and shown the quadratic-kernel ablation; A judged the original Fig. 6 and received copied baseline numbers instead.
No novelty verdict rested on a wrong account of prior work; aGgD's cursory comparison with Meinke and Hein is not shown to be wrong.
A's spotlight rests on a meta-review that gives no reason for the higher tier, and no A reviewer rated above 7 or argued for a spotlight.
The framing objections (z1y4 on 'BNN', 4z2v on infinite ReLU) are technical points within the field, not premises of a neighbouring field.
B's only champion (oTxs at 8) sat on the lower-tier committee, and A's reviewers engaged with the response; the mechanism does not explain the split.
Both committees accepted; no one judged the promised fixes too large for camera-ready.
Neither area chair cited an assessment outside the committee's record.
Both committees judged the paper as a theory-plus-method contribution under the same standard.
No below-threshold score was held; B's 6s are weak accepts, and 4z2v's rests on the central DSCS motivation, not a peripheral point.
